# Test fixtures

Committed on purpose, and small on purpose.

## `tiny.onnx` (285 bytes)

A two-input, two-output ONNX graph — `ids` (i64) and `weights` (f32) echoed to
`ids_out` and `scores` through `Identity` nodes, with symbolic batch/sequence
dimensions.

**Regenerate** (writes both fixtures):

```sh
cargo run -p cf-gears-onnx-runner --features fixture-gen \
  --example generate_test_fixture
```

The generator prints each new SHA-256 and names the constant it belongs to;
update `FIXTURE_SHA256` / `OTHER_FIXTURE_SHA256` in `tests/common/mod.rs` to
match.

**Why it exists.** The gear's real models total 528 MB, are gitignored, and are
fetched on demand — so before this fixture, nothing in CI ran the gear against a
real ONNX session. `cargo test` passing meant very little.

**Why it is committed** rather than fetched. The constraint against model
artifacts in version control
(`cpt-cf-onnx-runner-constraint-model-artifacts-not-vcs`) is written about size:
"nothing that size enters version control", of artifacts totalling 528 MB. At
285 bytes this is consistent with that reasoning rather than an exception to it.

**A second use.** The generator emits arbitrary graphs, so a concurrency benchmark can
use it to produce a ladder of synthetic models with tunable compute cost — making compute
a controlled variable instead of inheriting whatever a real model happens to do. Keep it
general enough for that.

**Why two dtypes and two names.** So contract verification and typed extraction
are both meaningful: a test can declare the wrong dtype, or a name the graph
does not have, and see the right failure.

**Why `Identity`.** The graph is bit-stable on every platform, so tests assert
exact equality instead of picking a tolerance.

## `other.onnx` (307 bytes)

A second graph, and deliberately unlike the first in every dimension a per-model
contract can differ along: different tensor names (`tokens`/`marks` rather than
`ids`/`weights`), and the two dtypes `tiny.onnx` never exercises — `u8` and
`bool`.

**Why a second one exists.** Multi-model hosting is only meaningfully tested when
the two models *disagree*. Two copies of one graph would pass a
contract-isolation test that no isolation at all would also pass: every call
would succeed whichever model answered it. With these two, feeding one model's
tensors to the other is a typed rejection naming the model that refused them,
and that is an assertion worth making.

Regenerated by the same command as `tiny.onnx`, which writes both; the generator
prints each digest and which constant in `tests/common/mod.rs` it belongs to.

## `tokenizer.json` (~1 KB)

A minimal WordLevel tokenizer with a whitespace pre-tokenizer and
`[CLS]`/`[SEP]` template post-processing, so `encode` (special tokens) and
`encode_fragment` (no special tokens) are distinguishable.

Its vocabulary deliberately includes Cyrillic, CJK and accented entries, because
the offset tests need text whose byte length and character length differ.

Hand-written; there is no generator. Edit it directly.
